target_pattern: Use ser for identity, role, origin, relationships, and stable traits; avoid confusing it with estar for temporary states.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Using estar for every is/are sentence.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish uses ser for identity, origin, role, relationships, and stable traits.
natural_examples: Ellos son mis compañeros de trabajo.

controlled_recombination.instructions: Write each in Spanish using ser naturally. No answer key until the end.
prompts_en: The red house is my mother's.
I am from the United States.

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Soy estudiante. -> change to plural (nosotros).
Base: Ella es profesora. -> turn into question.
Base: Somos de México. -> change country to Colombia.
Base: Ellos son inteligentes. -> change to feminine plural.
Base: Mi casa es grande. -> make it negative.
Base: La película es interesante. -> change adjective to aburrida.
Base: Juan es carpintero. -> add adjective bueno correctly.
Base: María es profesora. -> add adjective excelente.
Base: ¿De dónde eres? -> answer with Canada.
Base: ¿Quién es ella? -> answer with my friend.
Base: El hombre es alto. -> change subject to plural.
Base: La mujer es amable. -> make it very kind.
Base: Nosotros somos compañeros de clase. -> change to they.
Base: El libro es aburrido. -> change to plural books.
Base: Soy de Estados Unidos. -> change to tú question.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the most natural pattern in Spanish.
prompts: I am tired right now. (estoy vs soy)
I am a patient person. (soy vs estoy)
She is from Peru. (es de vs está de)
The soup is hot right now. (está vs es)
The movie is boring in general. (es aburrida vs está aburrida)
Who is he? (¿quién es...? vs ¿quién está...?)
They are my friends. (son vs están) identity relationship.
The office is closed. (está cerrada vs es cerrada) temporary condition.
The car is red. (es rojo vs está rojo) color trait.
The banana is green (unripe). (está verde vs es verde) condition reading.

guided_personal_writing.instructions: Write one Spanish sentence for each specific meaning.
prompts: You are from your country and live in your city.
You are a professional in your field.
One friend of yours is very organized.
Your coworkers are friendly.
Your manager is demanding but fair.
Your neighborhood is quiet.
One meeting today is important.
One class you take is difficult but useful.
One person in your family is very funny.
Your favorite book is interesting.
You are not from Spain.
Two colleagues are from different countries.
One project of yours is ambitious.
One restaurant you like is expensive but good.
Your long-term goal is clear.

prompts_en: He's one of my best friends.
This is my first time here.
